author: irrigation_nation
review_text: The customization depth surprised me: swapped my Trowel-9's shoulder cannon for an irrigation drone bay, tuned the leg servos for soft soil, painted the whole thing sage green. Every farm chore has a mech solution and finding it is the game's real puzzle. Combat is thin, sure, but I've stopped caring — my drones water the rustwheat while I watch the sunrise from the cockpit.

author: prodigal_planter
review_text: Came back after a year away for the 2.0 Reforged update and it is everything the old roadmap promised and then some. Mythril forging tier, frostwheat winter crops, ranching, and an apology letter in the patch notes that made me weirdly emotional. The 14 month silence was rough and they clearly know it. All is forgiven, my hammer is busy again.

author: pawn_fodder
review_text: Rank 2 and I keep getting paired against actual grandmasters. Why.

author: photonfinish
review_text: Came back after patch 1.4 and the crashing is completely gone. Three-hour session last night, zero issues. Changing my review back to positive. The new drift ghosts feature is a great excuse to lose to yourself repeatedly.

author: coldtake_carl
review_text: Staggering ambition. Broken, beautiful, and unlike anything else.

author: tpose_witness
review_text: Every NPC in Frosthaven greeted me in T-pose like they were about to ascend. The Whiteout Protocol quest will not complete, the script just dies after the avalanche. Wait for patches.

author: forty_ton_farmer
review_text: Watered my rustwheat with a mech the size of a church. Inner peace achieved.

author: ragequit_rhino
review_text: This isn't 'brutal but fair', it's a dev laughing at you. Checkpoints are placed out of spite. Magnetron Prime took me 70 attempts and when it died I felt nothing but relief. Life is too short.

author: driftking_92
review_text: Still my favorite arcade racer this decade, but I CTD'd twice tonight in the middle of championship races. 1.3 broke something. Recommending anyway because the handling is that good, but save often and lower your expectations.

author: reef_returner
review_text: Patch 1.2 fixed the saves. Now the only thing eating my run is the anglerkin.

author: waityear_wendy
review_text: Come back in a year. Trust me and my broken save file.

author: lod_pls
review_text: A year and a half of patches and large castles still chug. The optimization pass helped, but the engine redraws every distant arrow slit as if I'm standing next to it. No level-of-detail system, no occlusion, so ambition gets punished with stutter. The creative tools are the best in the genre, which is exactly why this hurts. I'll come back when my keep stops running like a flipbook.

author: sleepy_udon
review_text: i came for the noodles i stayed for the vibes. no notes

author: moat_enjoyer
review_text: Finally a building sim that lets me be both architect and demolition crew. Rebuilt my hometown's fortress from memory, then took a contract to tear down a rival keep. Watching the curtain wall peel away in chunks never gets old.

author: cipher_stumped
review_text: Stuck two hours on the telegraph cipher before caving and opening a guide. The solution was clever in hindsight, but the game gives you almost nothing to work with. Still adored the rest.

author: penthouse_pauper
review_text: 121 hours, so take my thumbs down with a grain of salt. The core loop is great but the endgame is a treadmill: same shifts, same tickets, same three broths, forever. The roadmap teased an Endless Night mode over a year ago and we got a cat sticker pack instead. I burned out waiting. If you are fine with a 30 hour game, buy it today. Just do not expect it to keep growing.

author: cash_register_carl
review_text: Great game buried under a cash register.

author: lofi_slurp
review_text: The lo-fi soundtrack alone is worth the price. I leave the game running while I work just for the music. Broth Bros please sell the OST separately.

author: cul_de_sac_dad
review_text: My daughter and I take turns launching the ice cream truck. She's seven and calls it 'the yeet game'. Best 7 euros I've ever spent on our relationship.

author: sonar_scaredy
review_text: I have never been this scared by a game. The sonar ping mechanic means you hear things long before you see them, and what you hear is worse. Played entirely with the lights on. No regrets, some trauma.

author: dev_null_dumper
review_text: Piped an entire wave of malware sprites into /dev/null and felt like a god. Chained tail into grep to spot the hidden daemon spawning adds during the Kernel fight. Chmod'd a locked door to 777 and strolled through like it was nothing. Yes, the first five hours are a cliff face with no rope, and the game explains none of it. Climb anyway. The view from root is worth it.

author: pendulum_pat
review_text:
Pros:
- Pixel-perfect physics, best in the genre
- Level design keeps introducing new ideas for 30+ hours
- Soundtrack goes stupidly hard for a game about falling

Cons:
- Controller support has been 'beta' for over a year
- Magnetron Prime is a difficulty cliff, not a curve
- No assist options for the wrist-destroying later levels

Verdict: buy it, but bring a keyboard and patience.

author: tower_flipper
review_text: Slumlord simulator but make it whimsical. Fantastic.

author: spellcheck_absent
review_text: teh funniest managment game ive ever played, my gargoyle tennant keeps complaning about pidgeons and i cant stop reading his letters. definately worth the money

author: halloween_hype
review_text: Played it live for friends on Halloween. Four grown adults screamed at conditional formatting. The pause after it asks 'enable editing?' is the best comedic timing of the year. Short, yes, but an instant party classic.

author: anemone_crew
review_text: Last night we pulled off our greatest heist. Two of us baited the security drones around the Anemone's engine block while our rookie cut through the floor from a maintenance shaft, straight into the vault bay. Fifteen minutes of held breath on voice chat and one perfectly timed airlock cycle. No scripted mission, just systems colliding. This game creates stories. Bring three friends and some patience for the occasional disconnect.

author: pickle_prophet
review_text: Every session generates a story. Last night someone launched the Tower of Bologna across the kitchen, it landed fully assembled, and we all stood up like it was a sports final. The physics are just unpredictable enough to be funny and just consistent enough to master. Couch co-op gold, and online works fine too. Solo is skippable, buy it for game night.

author: patchwatch_petra
review_text: Patch 1.3 promised load time optimization. Loads went from 60 seconds to about 35 on my drive, so, progress, but still absurd for a turn based game. Everything else remains best in class.

author: fortress_fan
review_text: Credit where due: the Fortress anti-cheat update actually banned a visible wave of engine users, and my last twenty lobbies had maybe two suspicious players instead of ten. That's progress. The matchmaking still shoves fresh accounts against thousand-win veterans though, and low ranks are still bot city. Recommending it because the bones are brilliant and the devs finally seem awake, but they are not done.

author: permafrost_pete
review_text: The hunger and warmth systems interlock beautifully, and hunting caribou across cracking ice at night is genuinely tense. If Coldsnap keeps patching at this pace, this becomes a classic. Will be great in a year.

author: one_more_run_ok
review_text: 400+ hours. NOT recommended. Do you understand? I have a family. I have a job. And yet every night I'm back in the Mossy Cellar telling myself one more run. The turnip familiar knows me better than my coworkers do. I can't stop playing. Send help.

author: chaos_castling
review_text: Chess but the floor is lava and everyone has a knife. Yes.

author: airlock_annie
review_text: Disconnects every twenty minutes like clockwork. Lost a full hold of platinum scrap when the server dropped us mid-extraction. My crew moved on to other games and honestly I don't blame them.

author: lilguysenjoyer
review_text: the little guys. the LITTLE GUYS. i grew a radish paladin and cired when he sacrificed himself for my strawberry mage. game of the year, no notes

author: content_drought_dan
review_text: Fantastic for about 25 hours, then the content completely dries up. No seasonal events, no new floors since the 1.4 patch, nothing to chase. Thumbs down until they feed the endgame something.

author: apogee_runner
review_text: 600 hours, most of them chasing leaderboard times in Kepler Junction. The reason this game holds up: the physics are deterministic. Same input, same result, every single time, which is why the speedrun scene is thriving. And yes — the 1.5 patch finally got controller support out of beta, and it actually works now, deadzones and all. Took them long enough, but this is the definitive way to play.

author: nitr0nadia
review_text: game dies after the update at least once a night, usualy mid drift. still cant quit it tho. the handling has ruined every other racer for me. plz fix velocity forge

author: q3_budget_ghost
review_text: A haunted quarterly budget that whispers your expense report back at you. The pivot-table jump scare got me so badly my cat left the room. Two hours of the funniest horror writing in years.

author: brickbybrick_ben
review_text: Once your castle passes five hundred pieces the frame rate falls off a cliff. My dream fortress became a lag fortress. The physics is glorious, the performance is authentically medieval.

author: fomo_fatigue
review_text: fomo pass, login queue, whale food. im out.

author: midday_medium
review_text: Beat it on a long lunch break and then thought about it for a week straight. Short? Absolutely. But every minute is dense with jokes and dread. Some meals are small and perfect.

author: grep_reaper
review_text: grep is a weapon here. literally. i grep the ghosts.

author: paywall_patrol
review_text: Half the units are paywalled. The Iron Choir pack alone costs 15 euro on top of a 25 euro game, and ranked is miserable without those units. A predatory model wrapped around brilliant design.

author: first_mate_finn
review_text: Launch-era pirate life is great. Four friends on a brig, someone yelling about the mainsail, cannonballs skipping across the waves. The cash shop is just hats for now. Come sail while it's still pure.

author: thirty_deaths_in
review_text: There is no tutorial. None. You wake up in a shell with a blinking cursor and the game just watches you drown. I died thirty times before learning I could even change directories. Some people call that design. I call it a wall.

author: CAPSLOCK_CORSAIR
review_text: THE ADMIRAL'S VAULT UPDATE IS THE LAST STRAW. RANDOMIZED CANNON CRATES WITH ACTUAL STAT BOOSTS. A GHOST CANNON THAT COSTS ROUGHLY FIFTY EURO AFTER THE GEM CONVERSION SANK MY FULLY CREWED BRIG IN TWO SHOTS. TWO. THREE YEARS OF LOYALTY AND KRAKEN INTERACTIVE TURNED A PIRATE GAME INTO A CASINO WITH SAILS. REVIEW STAYS NEGATIVE UNTIL THE CRATES SINK.

author: longthaw_lament
review_text: Third quest in a row where the script simply gave up. Talked to the elder, nothing. Reloaded, nothing. Rolled back my save and lost two hours. The writing is actually good, which somehow makes it hurt more.

author: walletfrost
review_text: 34.99 for what is essentially a paid beta is insulting. Half the systems are placeholders and the other half are frozen, and not in the fun thematic way. Massively overpriced for the state it shipped in.

author: orbit_owl
review_text: one more try turned into 3am again. the physcis are just so good

author: fps_accountant
review_text: RTX 4070, 32GB RAM, and Frosthaven still drops to 38fps in the market district. Quest markers corrupt after every fast travel and point at coordinates that do not exist, and The Long Thaw softlocked when an NPC froze mid dialogue. I want to love this so badly. The bones are genius. The flesh is missing. Come back at version 1.5.

author: case_reopened
review_text: The best-written game I've played in years. Every conversation with Inspector Vell crackles, every loop of the 4:17 reset teaches you something new about the same ten minutes, and the way the case slowly rearranges itself in your head is masterful. And the ending — I can't spoil it, but wow. I sat through the credits in silence and then immediately messaged three friends to buy it.

author: cost_per_laugh
review_text: Let's be honest, the novelty wears thin around hour three. But it costs less than a cinema ticket and I laughed more. The math checks out.

author: glacierbase_gus
review_text: Built my base into the side of a crevasse and rigged geothermal heating, then a patch moved the vent and my bedroom became a freezer. I laughed and rebuilt. That is this game: it breaks constantly and I keep coming back, because nothing else lets you homestead a living glacier. Flawed, ambitious, and slowly getting fixed.

author: regex_redemption
review_text: This game taught me regex better than two semesters of university. I captured a boss's attack pattern with a grouping expression and my hands were shaking. Educational software disguised as a nightmare, or possibly the other way around.

author: typo_tactician
review_text: increadible tactics game, teh echo system is genius and evrey mission feels handcrafted. deepest stratagy ive played in years, definately recomended for patient players

author: afterthought_alert
review_text: Single player is clearly an afterthought, a spreadsheet wearing a chef hat. But with friends this is the loudest fun in the genre, so thumbs up with an asterisk the size of a baguette.

author: coffee_spill_carol
review_text: the pivot table jump scare made me spill coffee on my actual work spreadsheet. hazard pay for this game please. anyway 10/10, hr has been notified

author: runtime_police
review_text: Finished in one hour fifty-four. Even at ten euro that stings when the store page says nothing about length. Brilliant concept, criminally brief. Wait for a sale or a content update.

author: annex_archivist
review_text: The Records Annex at closing time, rain on the windows, a case file that doesn't add up. This game understands atmosphere like nothing else in the genre.

author: okgardener
review_text: 200 hours. no regrets. okay, some regrets. one more run.

author: aurora_chaser
review_text: Climbed the Shiverspire at dawn, aurora overhead, ice groaning under my boots. Gorgeous frozen world, easily the best looking survival game out there. Buggy, sure, but I keep taking screenshots instead of surviving.

author: digital_sandcastles
review_text: digital sandcastles with structural liability. deeply my thing.

author: refund_randy
review_text: hangs on the loading screen since the update. stared at neon for ten minutes.

author: vell_wisher
review_text: the writting in this game, my god. inspector vell lives in my head rent free

author: stutter_step
review_text: The spec sheet says 8GB of VRAM. Reality says 12. Constant texture streaming stutter on my 3060 Ti, 40fps dropping to 15 whenever a new zone loads in. Terrifying atmosphere, mostly because of the frame graph.

author: voidjanitor
review_text: Drifting through a dead freighter in Sector 7 with three friends on voice chat, flashlights cutting through the dust, somebody whispering that the reactor is still warm. Best co-op atmosphere in years. Play it with a full crew.

author: fernfriend
review_text: Endgame gets grindy, no way around it. Unlocking the last greenhouse tier took me thirty hours of running the same three biomes. But the moment-to-moment gardening combat is so pleasant I barely minded. Mostly.

author: roadmap_mourner
review_text: No update in 14 months. Fourteen. The game is wonderful and abandoned, like a beautiful barn nobody repairs. I cannot recommend a live game that is not alive.

author: moatdigger600
review_text: i dig moats to relax. six hundred hours of moats.

author: walkthrough_walt
review_text: Honest review: I had a walkthrough tab open for the entire final act, and I don't feel guilty about it. The pneumatic mail-sorting puzzle alone must have ended careers. But here's the thing — even being dragged through it by a guide, this is one of the best detective stories in the medium. The writing carries everything. Imagine what it would be with a proper hint system.

author: slingshot_sue
review_text: Playing on my living room TV there's a noticeable delay between pressing jump and the little guy actually jumping — feels like half a second on bad days. I eventually moved to my desk monitor and the game transformed. And what a game it is under there: momentum puzzles, the Slingshot Gauntlet, a soundtrack that ramps up as you fall. Fix the latency and this is a classic.

author: wax_and_wane
review_text:
Pros:
- Best hand-drawn art in the genre, and it's not close
- A soundtrack that will live in your head for months
- Bosses that feel like duels, not stat checks
- A story that earns its ending

Cons:
- The map is decorative spaghetti
- Fast travel unlocks hours later than it should
- One nasty difficulty spike in the Gloaming

Still an easy recommendation.

author: under_the_map_andy
review_text: Incredible immersive experience. I am currently beneath the glacier, falling gently through infinite blue nothing, watching a T-posing seal spin past me. Truly next gen. 10/10, would clip through reality again.

author: timetable_terror
review_text: Stuck 90 minutes on the tram timetable puzzle. The answer was on a poster two rooms back. Rude. Brilliant, but rude. The new Consultant Mode hints would have saved me — I just refused to use them out of pride.

author: quiet_flame
review_text: Haunting. That's the word. Haunting.

author: camera_casualty
review_text: Two problems: alone there is nothing to do, and the swooping camera gave me a headache before I could even find someone to play with. Not for solo players, and possibly not for inner ears.

author: sandbox_convert
review_text: The new practice sandbox in 1.2 should have shipped at launch, but credit where due: consequence-free shell, searchable in-game manual, and suddenly my non-programmer partner is clearing floor three. Complaints addressed, thumbs up.

author: pros_cons_pipe
review_text:
Pros:
- real shell commands, pipes and all, as core mechanics
- proper roguelike depth, seeded runs, dailies
- chiptune soundtrack that goes way too hard

Cons:
- throws you off the deep end with zero explanation
- permadeath plus typos equals heartbreak
- inventory is literally environment variables, which is funny until it isn't

For terminal people this is a 10. Everyone else, start in sandbox mode.

author: queue_sailor
review_text: spent longer in the login queue than in the actual tutorial.

author: turn_based_tina
review_text:
Pros:
- Every turn is a genuine puzzle
- The echo mechanic is the freshest tactics idea in a decade
- Fantastic map variety

Cons:
- Load times are absurd even on an SSD
- Too many units locked behind DLC
- The menu music will colonize your brain

author: first_crown_frank
review_text: Seventy hours to win my first crown. I stood up and screamed at 1am. My neighbors hate me and it was completely worth it.

author: one_more_queue
review_text: 463 hours. NOT recommended. The matchmaking is a coin flip, half my lobbies are bots on rails, and an engine user ruins every third final circle. Anyway, I'm queuing again tonight. I can't stop. Send help.

author: HundredHourHannah
review_text: 218 hours and every run still surprises me. The seed synergy system is deceptively deep: sunflower turret plus dew charm plus the sprint trowel turns you into a lawnmower of love. My only real complaint after all this time is the inventory. Twelve slots was fine in year one, but there are so many seed types now that half my run is bag management. Give us pockets, Tiny Cauldron.

author: moth_mum
review_text: The Mother Pyralis fight, with that lullaby playing underneath it? I put the controller down afterwards and just sat there. Games don't usually do that to me.

author: cliff_climber_cs
review_text: People say difficulty curve. This is a difficulty cliff, sheer and frictionless. But the moment piping finally clicked and I one-shot a floor that used to take twenty minutes, no game has ever felt more rewarding.

author: keyboard_krusader
review_text: I have thrown my headset once, slapped my desk more times than I can count, and developed an eye twitch that activates whenever I hear the respawn sound. My hands hate this game. Recommending it anyway, because apparently I hate my hands.

author: frame_perfect_fiona
review_text: There is visible input latency on my setup — press jump, count to half a second, watch him leap into a laser. Tried three cables, two monitors, borderless and fullscreen. A precision game that ignores your inputs isn't hard, it's broken.

author: saltiest_veteran
review_text: Eleven hundred hours since the 2022 launch, so believe me when I say I wanted to love this forever. Watch the timeline: 2022, cosmetics only. 2023, XP boosts appear. 2024, the battle pass grows expiring tiers. 2025, gacha cannons with stats. Every year the ship battles stay brilliant and every year they get buried under another storefront. The login queue is even back on event weekends. I'm done. o7

author: moss_witch_maja
review_text: The most wholesome roguelite ever made. You grow a little vegetable knight, you bonk slugs, you die, your garden remembers you. I meant to play for twenty minutes and it is now dawn.

author: wavegarage
review_text: 1.4 runs smooth as glass now. soundtrack still undefeated.

author: foreshadow_hunter
review_text: Second playthrough finished. Knowing the ending, the foreshadowing is everywhere — background dialogue, the clock faces, even the stamps on the case files. It's all there from minute one, hidden in plain sight, and I refuse to say more because you deserve to find it clean. Puzzle difficulty is still spiky (Consultant Mode helps now), but as a piece of writing this is the finest detective fiction in games.

author: ng_plus_nancy
review_text: New game plus adds three endings and a secret one hidden behind a formula I won't spoil. Hunting them doubled my playtime, and the sinister-cheerful tone never wears out. The short-game complaints are officially outdated.

author: map_button_where
review_text: The cash shop button is bigger than the map button. That's the whole review. That's the entire design philosophy in one screenshot.

author: wok_this_way
review_text: Wish there was anything past the penthouse floor. You max everything out and the game politely runs out of ideas. Still one of my favorite chill games ever made, hence the thumb up.

author: ping_999
review_text: 5/5, the desync adds roguelike unpredictability. You never know which deck you're actually standing on, or whether the loot you grabbed exists. Schrodinger's salvage. My friends and I have started betting on whose reality is canon. Thumbs up, I guess.

author: cozygrind
review_text: cozy on the outside, crippling addiction on the inside.

author: abyssal_completionist
review_text: 84 hours, every log collected, new game plus finished after 1.2. Saves have been rock solid since the patch. This is the best survival horror in years and I will not be elaborating on what lives in the Brinefall.

author: goatnado_survivor
review_text: The 9.3 Goatnado update is the funniest patch ever shipped. Sixty goats in one tornado, a physics engine audibly begging for death, my fps in the single digits, and I did not care even a little.

author: honest_hoagie
review_text: Buy this if and only if you have people to play with. Solo mode feels like practicing a wedding dance alone in a garage. With a full couch it is an absolute riot.

author: broadside_bros
review_text: Nothing in gaming beats a coordinated broadside. Four of us with roles locked in: helm, sails, cannons, repairs. We chased a rival crew through a storm into the Kraken's Maw event, traded volleys around the whirlpool, and boarded them with two hull planks left. The cash shop is creeping toward pay-for-power and the queues on event nights are grim, but when this game sings, it SINGS.

author: refund_speedrun
review_text: Fell through the ice four times in the tutorial. Refunded.

author: doubloon_doubter
review_text: the real treasure was the microtransactions we bought along the way.

author: desync_dave
review_text: The desync is unreal. My buddy watched me float outside the hull while on my screen I was cutting cargo straps. We sold the same salvage twice and then it vanished for both of us. Great game trapped inside terrible netcode.

author: adventure_grump
review_text: Moon logic everywhere. At one point the answer is basically 'combine the stamp with the pigeon' and I refuse to believe anyone solved that unaided. Great prose, exhausting puzzles.

author: faithful_farmer
review_text: The Reforged update saved this game. Welcome back, Anvil and Acre.

author: FROZEN_AND_FURIOUS
review_text: 35 EURO FOR THIS. THE MAIN QUEST BROKE TWO HOURS IN, THE OBJECTIVE MARKER SENT ME TO AN EMPTY IGLOO, AND WHEN I FAST TRAVELED BACK THE ENTIRE VILLAGE WAS T-POSING AT ME LIKE A CULT. THEN I FELL THROUGH THE ICE AND KEPT FALLING. FOREVER. INTO THE VOID. COLDSNAP TESTED NOTHING. DO NOT BUY UNTIL THIS IS FIXED.

author: one_evening_wonder
review_text: Great with friends watching, but solo the novelty runs dry fast. I saw basically everything it has in one evening. Fun evening though.

author: turnip_tamer
review_text: Grandma Bramble is the best first boss in the genre. She knits while she fights you and apologizes when she wins. Also my turnip familiar has a little hat now. Ten out of ten.

author: spoiler_vault
review_text: I can't spoil it, but WOW. Go in blind.

author: autosum_scream
review_text: Perfect horror-comedy rhythm. It lulls you with a joke about expense categories, then the autosum row starts summing numbers you never entered. I laughed and screamed within the same five seconds. More games should be this confident.

author: papercut_prophet
review_text: Bring tissues, and a notebook for directions.

author: quiet_quencher
review_text: watered my crops, hammered a sword, felt feelings. perfect game

author: weekend_sysadmin
review_text: I administer servers for a living and now, apparently, for fun. The Cron Reaper boss spawns adds on a real schedule you can read and edit if you're fast enough, which is the cleverest fight design I've seen in years. My wife asked why I was killing processes at midnight and I had to clarify it was recreational. The learning curve filtered out my whole friend group though. I alone remain.

author: arcane_accountant
review_text: 82 hours in and the writing still surprises me. A banshee formed a tenant union with three skeletons and their list of demands made me cry laughing. Yes, the Mimic Chest exploit still works even after patch 1.2 claimed to fix it, and yes, gold is basically decorative at this point, but I stopped caring. I am here for the letters. Arcane Lease, hire more writers and fire your economist.

author: leaselich
review_text:
Pros:
- Sharpest comedy writing in the genre
- Complaint letters I screenshot and send to friends
- Evicting a poltergeist is a whole quest line

Cons:
- Gold stops mattering by week 3
- Tenant AI walks into walls and occasionally into each other
- The rent formula appears to be a random number generator

author: vsync_vera
review_text: PSA: if your inputs feel laggy, turn off vsync and cap the framerate in the config file. Went from mushy to instant on my 1660, solid 144fps. Game is a masterpiece once it actually listens to you.

author: crumb_collider
review_text: 9/10 would clip through Mayor Crumb again. Docked one point: he clipped through me first.

author: quiet_thinker
review_text: Chess energy. My brain hums after every mission.

author: one_button_bored
review_text: Combat is mashing one button against the same three chrome aphids, over and over. The farming half is lovely, but half a game is exactly what this is.

author: verdigris_veteran
review_text: 210 hours. The endgame is thin and I've automated almost everything, but the ritual keeps pulling me back — morning rounds in the mech, checking mutation crops from the Harvest Protocol update, rain on the hull. The new weather system genuinely changed how I plan my seasons. Combat still needs a real rework and the roadmap is behind, but this is my comfort game and I've accepted it.

author: laptop_lava
review_text: my laptop sounds like a trebuchet winding up whenever i load my big castle. 12 fps in the courtyard, 40 in an empty feild. love the game, cant actualy play the game

author: breathing_walls
review_text: i heard something breathe behind me and unplugged my headphones. masterpiece.

author: four_seventeen
review_text: The moment the 4:17 loop structure clicks and you realize what the game has been doing the whole time — chills. Actual chills. Smartest structure in the genre.

author: budget_build_ben
review_text: My 8GB card chokes hard — 22fps on medium at 1080p with VRAM pegged the entire time. A 3070 should not be struggling like this in corridors. Wait for optimization.

author: ferris_wheel_felon
review_text: Strapped a jetpack to my goat, crashed a wedding, got the bride's bouquet stuck to my tongue, dragged the entire buffet table up the ferris wheel, and then the ragdoll physics flung me three districts away into an open manhole. The game gave me an achievement called 'Uninvited'. I have not laughed this hard at a screen in years. It is deeply stupid and I love it.

author: duct_tape_dev
review_text: Great jokes stapled to an economy made of wet cardboard.

author: lostcargo_lena
review_text: Session died during the final haul of a three-hour run and the game kept nothing. No reconnect, no recovery, just a menu screen and my crew groaning on voice chat. Until they fix connection stability, wait.

author: cello_ghost
review_text: the gloaming at dusk with the cello theme. i wept. actually wept.

author: diesel_daisy
review_text: Piloting a 40-ton mech to gently water tomato rows should not work as a concept, and yet it's the most relaxing thing I've played all year. Iron Petal understood something the rest of us didn't.

author: sub_zero_sub
review_text: Nine euro for this much screaming is a bargain.

author: bored_bovid
review_text: Everything funny happens in the first two hours. After that it's an empty sandbox and you realize the jokes were the whole game. There's no there there.

author: analog_andy
review_text: The analog stick deadzone is all wrong. Tiny movements get ignored, then it suddenly registers full tilt — in a game about millimeter-perfect jumps that's fatal. The 1.4.2 beta patch improved it slightly, but it still feels like steering a shopping cart.

author: hydrophone_hermit
review_text: Wear headphones. The sound design is the best I have ever heard — the hull groans, the distant sonar returns, the wet clicking the anglerkin make when they're close. There's a chase through Deck C of the Meridian that I had to pause halfway through just to breathe. The scariest game of the decade when it works, and it mostly works.

author: gauntlet_glenn
review_text: The Slingshot Gauntlet is the best platforming level ever made. Fight me.

author: lone_lettuce
review_text: Solo mode is a snoozefest. The fun only exists in multiplayer.

author: friendship_ruiner
review_text: Terrible game. It has ruined three friendships, my sister no longer speaks to me after the mustard incident, and we have played every single Friday for four months straight. Absolutely do not buy it. Five stars, thumbs up.

author: turing_test_ted
review_text: Lobby full of bots. Sixty of my 99 opponents moved instantly with zero blunders until they all collapsed on cue, and then the same three usernames show up in every real match. The player count is smoke and mirrors.

author: zone_hitch
review_text: Genuinely great horror, but I can't recommend it until they optimize. There's a massive hitch every time you cross into a new zone — nothing kills terror like a two-second freeze mid-chase.

author: certified_coward
review_text: 0.9 hours played. Refunded. Not because it's bad — because I'm a coward.

author: ClutchKickCarla
review_text: Great racing, gorgeous neon rain effects, and the drifting feels like butter on Sunset Loop. Only gripe is the rubber-band AI. You can drive a perfect race and second place still magnetizes to your bumper on the final straight.

author: couch_gamer_carl
review_text: Keyboard only, sadly. Two years on and pad support is still half-broken.

author: qa_goat
review_text: Bug report: goat clips through the town hall, physics explode, save intact, dignity gone. Dev response in the patch notes: 'working as intended'. Bless Chaos Pasture. Never change.

author: pressure_hull_poet
review_text: The story is told mostly through the Meridian's logs and it's quietly devastating — a crew that knew what was coming and wrote letters anyway. The dread here isn't jump scares, it's pressure: the hull, the dark, the fuel gauge on the dive suit. Few games commit to an atmosphere this completely. Buy a VRAM-rich GPU first, though.

author: lumen_seeker
review_text: I don't cry at games. I cried at this one. Every frame of the hand-drawn art looks like it took someone a week, the Wax Cathedral is the most beautiful area I've seen in the genre, and the score — this quiet, aching cello thing — follows you around like a second character. The final hour broke me. Some map frustrations aside, an absolute triumph.

author: noodle_gremlin
review_text: One more shift turned into 3am again. This game is dangerously addictive and I refuse to apologize for my behavior.

author: silence_smith
review_text: Radio silence from the developers for over a year now. No patches, no posts, nothing. I cannot in good conscience tell anyone to buy into what looks like abandonware, no matter how good the forging feels.

author: hollow_wanderer
review_text: I spent more time lost than fighting. The in-game map looks like abstract art — beautiful, useless. Recommended anyway, because everything else is close to perfect.

author: crews_control
review_text: New player here with a crew of friends, honestly having a blast without paying a cent. Yes, the veterans are right about the shop, you feel it in PvP. But casual ship battles with your mates? Still genuinely special.

author: quietbloom
review_text: I picked this up during a rough patch of my life and it was exactly what I needed. Nothing in it is cruel. You lose a run and the game plants a memorial flower where you fell. I've since beaten everything, hit the late-game grind wall everyone mentions, and I still log in just to water things. The inventory could be bigger. The heart could not.

author: student_la_poli
review_text: sincer m-a invatat pipe-uri si redirectari mai bine decat laboratorul de la facultate. nu are tutorial deloc si primele ore sunt crunte, dar cand iti iese primul one-liner care curata tot etajul... satisfactie maxima. il recomand la toti colegii

author: barnfresh
review_text: Bought it right after the big 2.0 update. Zero regrets.

author: thumbstick_theo
review_text: Refunded. My gamepad straight up isn't detected — tried two different pads, replugged, restarted, nothing. The forums are full of the same complaint. A precision platformer on keyboard is not what I paid for.

author: eggtimer_ela
review_text: Bought it at lunch, missed two meetings. 10/10.

author: sahist_suparat
review_text: Ideea e geniala, sah cu 100 de oameni pe aceeasi tabla uriasa, ce sa zic. Dar la fiecare doua meciuri dau peste unul care joaca clar cu motor, muta in doua secunde si numai mutari perfecte. Plus ca matchmaking-ul m-a bagat cu unul de rating 2400 cand eu abia stiu deschiderile. Pacat, chiar pacat.

author: bread_believer
review_text: me and the boys yelling about pastrami for six hours straight. goty

author: lowercase_mage
review_text: rented a swamp to a frog wizard and he sued me. game of the year

author: broth_veteran
review_text: 310 hours. I have memorized every ticket chime. Is it repetitive once you clear floor 30? Sure. Do I care? The lo-fi hits, the noodles fly, I am at peace.

author: boarded_by_wallets
review_text: Skill stopped mattering the day stat gear hit the shop. We got boarded by wallet warriors in gilded armor doing double damage and shrugging off ours. We were better sailors. They were better spenders. Guess who won.

author: glowberry_gardener
review_text: My evening routine now: clock off work, boot up, stomp the Trowel-9 out to the glowberry field, harvest while the sun sets over Verdigris Valley, listen to the rain start on the cockpit glass. That's it. That's the game. There's combat in there somewhere too, and it's fine, whatever — I'm here to be a giant robot with a watering can and be at peace.

author: rm_rf_freetime
review_text: sudo rm -rf my free time.

author: TonkotsuTruther
review_text: Late game is literally Midnight Miso, Neon Tonkotsu and Spicy Sunrise on rotation forever. Same three recipes on loop until the heat death of the universe. Love the game, but my hands are on autopilot now.

author: caffeine_castle
review_text: free, brilliant, infuriating. the holy trinity.

author: lastlap_larry
review_text: The AI doesn't race, it teleports. You can lead by six seconds and the pack will still appear in your mirrors on the last lap like a horror movie. Rubber-banding this aggressive makes clean driving pointless.

author: moonwalk_mike
review_text: rubber-banding so bad my character moonwalked through the airlock and into next week.

author: wintersale_victim
review_text: got it in the winter sale, lost the entire winter.

author: tongue_physics
review_text: i licked a car and draged it into the sea. game of the yaer

author: party_planner_pia
review_text: Bought four copies for game night and it paid for itself in one evening. Simple to learn, impossible to play with dignity. The sandwich physics alone justify the price tag.

author: cozy_conjurer
review_text: Perfect evening game. Collect rent, read letters, laugh out loud, renovate a haunted attic, repeat. For 13.99 you get more genuine laughs than most comedy specials.

author: hallway_hoverer
review_text: Played with every light in my flat on and a friend on voice call for moral support. Still had to stop every twenty minutes. Incredible game, hostile to my heart rate.

author: siege_the_day
review_text: Nobody talks about the siege testing mode enough. You finish your castle, then the game hands you catapults and lets you find out whether your design was clever or merely decorative. My east tower folded like wet parchment because I'd skimped on foundations, and the collapse rippled exactly where the load paths said it should. This is an engineering toy wearing a castle costume and I adore it.

author: demo_price_tag
review_text: two hours long. that's a demo with a price tag.

author: post_shift_pilot
review_text: The game I play after work to feel like a person again. Cheaper than a therapist, and the tomatoes don't judge me.

author: no_challenge_ned
review_text: Once you crack the economy, and that takes about one in-game week, there is no challenge left. Currency loses all meaning and every decision becomes purely cosmetic. This needed a hard mode a year ago.

author: wreck_diver_wes
review_text: bought it for co-op night. we spent the evening staring at the reconnect screen.

author: man_page_meta
review_text: finally a game where reading the man page is the meta.

author: imp_watcher
review_text: My imp tenants spend rent day walking face first into the same wall for hours. The pathfinding is a crime scene. Still funny though, one of them has worn a visible groove into the plaster.

author: gravity_optional
review_text: Clipped through Mayor Crumb, got launched clean over Bleatsburg, landed in the trampoline church, achievement popped. This game understands what games are for.

author: compost_connoisseur
review_text: The Compost King fight is a masterpiece, a giant grump made of everything you discarded during the run. Died to my own banana peels. The 2.1 update's bigger inventory fixed my main gripe too.

author: null_warden_main
review_text: The unit roster is a toybox for sickos. My Null Warden erases enemy echoes while the Chronomancer replays her own turn from two rounds ago, and stacking those two won me a match I had mathematically lost. The campaign difficulty curve is perfect and the weekly puzzle missions are genius. Base roster is thin though, the really good stuff hides in DLC packs.

author: sandbox_skeptic
review_text: A mile wide and an inch deep. No goals, no progression, no reason to come back once the chaos stops being surprising — and it stops surprising you around hour three.

author: stomp_nap
review_text: plant. stomp. nap. repeat. best routine in gaming

author: apexghost77
review_text: The drift handling is the best I've felt in an arcade racer. You feather the throttle, the back end swings out, and the synthwave beat drops right as you hit the apex on Chromatic Bay. Velocity Forge understood the assignment.

author: patience_expired
review_text: I defended this game for months but I am done waiting. The promised ranching update is over a year late and the devs have not said a single word since last winter. Uninstalling until they remember we exist.

author: solo_sadness
review_text: Played alone and there is just nothing here. An empty score chase, no story, barely any progression. This game without friends is a sandwich without bread.

author: fiscal_fear_fan
review_text: Came back for the free Fiscal Year of Fear chapter and it finally makes the runtime feel fair. The year-end audit sequence is the scariest thing I've played in 2025, and I mean the horror parts, not just the audit itself.

author: ghosttown_gardener
review_text: The roadmap is a ghost town and the last dev post was a pumpkin emoji in January. I adore this game, 156 hours says so, but somebody please go check on Anvil and Acre.

author: anvil_lifer
review_text: 612 hours since launch. This game taught my kid crop rotation and taught me patience. The farming and forging loop is still unmatched. The problem: total dev silence. No patch since January 2025, the official roadmap page literally 404s now, and the community channel is a tumbleweed farm. I still recommend it for the mountain of content that exists, but my heart is getting nervous.

author: ticket_no_reply
review_text: Save file vanished after a crash on Deck C. My support ticket has been open for three weeks with no reply. The game is scary, losing eight hours is scarier.

author: accountant_ama
review_text: accountants: this is a documentary.

author: o2_optional
review_text: The sound design deserves an award. When your oxygen line snags and the hiss starts, and your friends' voices tip from jokes into panic, that's real fear. Solo it's decent, with three friends it's unforgettable.

author: daily_quest_dropout
review_text: The Sea Serpent pass turned my hobby into a shift job. Miss two days of streak quests and the tier math means you'll never finish without paying. I sailed for fun once. Now I clock in. No thanks.

author: rook_and_roll
review_text: Chess but it's a 100-player knife fight. Watching two top-tier players slug it out in the final circle while 98 ghosts spectate is genuinely the best moment in games right now. Concept of the decade.

author: second_chance_sam
review_text: Came back after the review bombing calmed down. The 1.1 patch fixed the corrupted markers and I have not fallen through the ice once in twenty hours. Still rough around the edges, but the turnaround is real.

author: vaporware_valley
review_text: Truly visionary studio. Lesser devs deliver features — Iron Petal delivers announcements of features. Raid Blooms has been 'coming next season' for three consecutive seasons, which for a farming game I assume is intentional comedy. The roadmap is the longest-growing crop in the game. Inspirational, really. 11/10.

author: chuckle_warlock
review_text: The tenant complaint letters alone are worth 14 euro.

author: slipstream_sue
review_text: Runs at a locked 144 fps on my four-year-old Vortex 3600, looks like a neon fever dream, and the drift chaining on Chromatic Bay never gets old. Easy recommendation at this price.

author: echo_addict
review_text: Every turn is a puzzle. Believe the hype.

author: seasonal_sal
review_text: The autumn festival made me tear up a little. Farm and Forge understands coziness on a level most games never reach, and the forging minigame has real depth. My hammer timing has become a personality trait.

author: pixelpetunia
review_text: Three years after release and Tiny Cauldron still ships free content updates with handwritten patch notes. This studio deserves every euro. The game remains the coziest possible way to ruin a sleep schedule.

author: mirceapofta
review_text: Joc perfect dupa o zi lunga la birou. Pui muzica lo-fi, faci un Midnight Miso, servesti trei clienti grabiti si uiti de toate. Merita banii lejer, poate devine putin repetitiv dupa etajul 30, dar sincer nu ma deranjeaza deloc.

author: HairpinHera
review_text: I was 40 hours in and hosting weekly time-trial nights with my club. Since the update the game freezes mid-race, always on Midnight Interchange, always around the tunnel section. Screen locks up, the music keeps playing, then nothing. I've lost three tournament runs to this. The driving underneath is still fantastic, which somehow makes it worse. Fix it and I'll flip this review.

author: cartography_crow
review_text: Fair warning: the map is genuinely confusing and you will get lost in the early hours. Push through anyway. Once the world finally clicks into place in your head, this becomes something special.

author: budget_astronaut
review_text: friend pass means my whole squad plays on one copy. based devs.

author: wet_paper_warrior
review_text: The farming is 10/10. The fighting is a wet paper towel.

author: eval_bar_victim
review_text: Queued at rank 3, got dismantled by someone who was streaming with an eval bar open on their second monitor. Reported them a week ago. They're still in my lobbies.

author: rain_on_the_hull
review_text: The rain sound on the cockpit hull deserves its own award. Cozy is an overused word, but this game earned it. Just don't come here for the combat.

author: grandmaster_grid
review_text: The deepest tactics system in years, full stop. Echo positioning means every unit's past turns literally haunt the battlefield, so you are playing against your own history as much as the enemy. Every turn is a puzzle with three wrong answers and one beautiful one. I have 132 hours and I am still discovering interactions. Thinky players, this is your game.

author: chewing_gum_chaos
review_text: Physics engine held together with chewing gum and dreams. Perfect.

author: shanty_singer
review_text: free to play, pay to win, hard to quit, uninstalled anyway.

author: ram_jam_2000
review_text: Headbutted a funeral procession into the stratosphere. 10/10.

author: somnorosul_99
review_text: Cea mai frumoasa grafica pe care am vazut-o intr-un joc de genul asta. M-am ratacit vreo doua ore in Cinder Hollow ca harta e praf, dar sincer nici nu m-am suparat. Muzica m-a facut sa plang, pe bune. Il recomand cu incredere.

author: tactician_dorel
review_text: Cel mai bun joc de tactica pe ture din ultimii ani, pe bune, fiecare tura e un puzzle. Singura problema mare: loading-urile sunt lungi rau de tot, si asta pe SSD nou. Astept sa repare, dar il recomand oricum cu incredere.

author: GhostlapGary
review_text:
Pros:
- drift model with actual weight transfer, best in class
- synthwave soundtrack I now listen to while jogging
- track variety, Harbor Straight at night is art

Cons:
- since 1.3 the game locks up between races about once an hour
- rubber-band AI on Expert is insulting
- photo mode crops replays weird

Recommended, but wait for the stability patch if you're on the fence.

author: three_week_sail
review_text: As a free player I grinded three weeks for the storm sails. A whale buys them in three seconds with gems and gets the stat variant, which I literally cannot earn. That's not free to play, that's a demo of someone else's game.

author: theyre_back_barb
review_text: THEY'RE BACK. The Reforged update dropped out of nowhere and it is massive: Mythril tier, frostwheat, a whole ranching system. I owe the doomposters an apology, myself included.

author: cosmetic_defeat
review_text: 10/10 best credit card simulator on the seven seas. My ship is cosmetic, my defeats are not. Love queueing into a galleon whose sails cost more than my monitor. Truly the authentic experience of being robbed by pirates.

author: scrapbaron
review_text: Sixty-plus hours in. Ship upgrades give real progression, the friend pass keeps my rotating crew stocked, and post-overhaul the lag spikes are rare. Docking a fully upgraded hauler stuffed with contraband while the station scans you is peak tension.

author: wobbly_wife_guy
review_text: Heads up: the default camera shake made my wife queasy within minutes. The 1.1 patch added a toggle buried in accessibility settings, turn it off and the problem disappears completely. After that, flawless party game.

author: knight_owl_gm
review_text: Winning a 1v1 in the final circle with 97 people spectating is peak human experience.

author: patchnotesreader
review_text: The January netcode overhaul actually delivered. Movement is server-side now, rubber-banding is mostly gone, and we survived a host crash with the new reconnect. Still the odd lag spike, but it's night and day compared to launch.

author: backtrack_burnout
review_text: Wandered the same three corridors of Cinder Hollow for 40 minutes because the map tells you nothing. No fast travel until absurdly late, so every wrong turn costs ten minutes of backtracking. Gorgeous game, miserable navigation.

author: queasy_quitter
review_text: Refunded. The camera whips around every time you sprint between stations and within twenty minutes I was genuinely nauseous. No FOV slider, no camera smoothing at launch. My stomach wrote this review.

author: chashu_charlie
review_text:
Pros:
- Addictive shift loop that eats whole evenings
- Lo-fi soundtrack is a warm blanket
- 11.99 is a steal

Cons:
- Progression flatlines around floor 30
- Recipe variety runs out long before you do
- The rooftop cat cannot be petted (patch this in, Broth Bros)

author: endgame_enjoyer
review_text: The shrinking board is a stroke of genius. As the circle closes, entire files just fall into the void, and suddenly your careful positional setup means nothing because the d-file no longer exists. The late game becomes a desperate three-board scramble where a pawn is worth more than a queen was five minutes ago. Matchmaking needs work and cheaters exist, but the core design deserves every award.

author: InventoryTetris
review_text: The game showers you with forty seed types and gives you twelve inventory slots. Late game is a grind tunnel where every reward is a duplicate. I adore the art and the vibe, but my patience finally composted.

author: harvest_hana
review_text: The loop is perfect: grow it, smelt it, smith it, sell it, upgrade the farm, repeat. Forging your own scythe from ore you mined under your own turnip field is the kind of loop other games dream about. The seasonal festivals are lovely, the mine gets surprisingly spooky, and the soundtrack changes with the weather. An instant classic.

author: git_gud_gerbil
review_text: Everyone calling it unfair is telling on themselves. Every hazard is telegraphed, every death has a lesson, and the physics never once betrayed me in 100+ hours. Hardest game I own and also the most honest one.

author: wiki_tab_warrior
review_text: Refunded. Alt-tabbing to a community wiki every forty seconds is not gameplay, it's homework. There is zero onboarding for anyone who doesn't already live in a terminal. Knowing your audience is fine, but a single practice room would have kept me.

author: flower_box_mech
review_text: My mech has a flower box mounted on its shoulder cannon. GOTY.

author: floor30_refugee
review_text: The loop is genuinely hypnotic, upgrade the stove, unlock a floor, chase a perfect service. But once you hit floor 30 the game just stops. No new customers, no new stations, no reason to open the shop tomorrow. I kept playing out of habit for twenty more hours hoping something would happen. Nothing did. Still recommending because those first sixty hours were incredible, but Broth Bros needs to build an actual endgame.

author: solo_no_more
review_text: do not play this solo. i mean it. i spent 20 hours alone and thought it was mid, then two friends joined and it instantly became my game of the year. the anemone wreck at night, full crew, no music, just breathing. cinema

author: cryptkeeper_karen
review_text: A lich filed a complaint letter about the crypt being too damp for his scrolls and offered to pay rent in cursed bone china. The writing is untouchable. Funniest game I have played in years.

author: loading_screen_larry
review_text: My loading screens last longer than my turns. Ninety seconds into a mission, on an SSD, in a turn based game. I have read every loading screen tip twice by now. Fix the tech, then we can talk.

author: hoe_there
review_text: Cozy farming plus blacksmithing. Instantly comfortable.

author: roadmap_watcher
review_text: The roadmap promised Co-op Greenhouses for autumn 2025. It is now July 2026. Raid Blooms: also missing. I love this game, which is exactly why I'm reviewing it down until Iron Petal delivers what the store page promised.

author: sundaydriver_dan
review_text: bought it for the drifting, stayed for the synthwave.

author: gatehouse_gabe
review_text: knocked down my own gatehouse just to watch it crumble. worth every euro.

author: macro_seance_fan
review_text: The macro seance is an all-timer sequence: you record a macro to contact the intern who never logged off, and the game plays it back with one extra keystroke you didn't make. I yelped, then laughed, then checked my own spreadsheets for macros I don't remember writing. The VLOOKUP demon that follows you between sheets is great too. Yes, it's barely two hours long. I'm expensing my therapy anyway.

author: abandonware_alarm
review_text: Last patch was January 2025. Is this abandonware? Genuine question. Steam says the devs were last seen online sometime in the Cretaceous. Wonderful game, dead project.

author: patient_prospector
review_text: Underneath the jank is the most ambitious survival game I have played this decade. A living glacier that shifts every in-game week, dynamic frostbite, settlements that migrate when the ice cracks. Yes it is broken. Yes I recommend it anyway, the way you recommend a brilliant friend who is going through something. In a year this will be a masterpiece.

author: deli_dasher
review_text: Pure chaos. My friends are liabilities and I love them.

author: petal_to_the_metal
review_text: Adore the vibe, but let's be honest, the combat is an afterthought — enemies wander vaguely at you and evaporate. I'm hoping a patch gives it teeth. Everything else is a warm blanket.

author: fifty_move_grind
review_text:
Pros:
- Best strategy concept in years, period
- Final circles are pure adrenaline
- Genuinely free, no pay-to-win

Cons:
- Engine users survive every ban wave
- Low-rank lobbies padded with obvious bots
- Matchmaking pairs rank 2s with veterans
- Cosmetic grind is glacial

The knife-fight chess dream is real, it just needs a security team.

author: packet_ghost
review_text: atmosphere immaculate, netcode haunted. bring friends and lower your ping expectations.

author: budget_broth
review_text: For 12 euro this is absurd value. Runs on my ancient GTX 1050 laptop at a locked 60fps. Perfect little management game for people with bad computers and good taste.

author: empty_pasture
review_text: Hot take: the bugs being the content is exactly the problem. Once the trampoline church stops being funny — and it does — there's no game underneath. No progression, no escalation, just the same ragdoll punchline with different props. I kept playing hoping for depth that never came. Comedy games still need to be games.

author: dev_mind_reader
review_text: The puzzles don't want you to think, they want you to read the developer's mind. Bounced off after the third arbitrary roadblock. The writing deserved better puzzle design.

author: ramen_papa_88
review_text: realy good managment game, teh customers get crazy on floor 15+ and i love it. soundtrak is amazing, definately recomend to anyone who likes cooking games

author: golem_stuck_again
review_text: Tenant AI is genuinely dumb. My stone golem has been standing in the courtyard fountain for six in-game months and the imps queue single file into a decorative wall. Immersion, gone. Charm only carries it so far.

author: turbo_tomasz
review_text: Loved this game until patch 1.3. Now it crashes to desktop every second or third race, usually right when I'm about to set a personal best. Not touching it again until they fix it.

author: comet_snacker
review_text: The physics here are absurdly good. Momentum carries exactly how your brain expects, so every splat is 100% your fault. Beat the Tidal Locks after two evenings of pure stubbornness and felt like a genius. Just one more try, forever.

author: radial_menu_victim
review_text: The build menu fights you constantly. Doors are buried two submenus deep, the radial wheel forgets your last pick, and rebinding barely works. I recommend the game anyway, because what you can make with it is worth the wrestling.

author: relit_lantern
review_text: Second full playthrough, this time after update 1.1, and what a difference — map pins, a cleaner legend, and the first bench-warp moved several hours earlier. The getting-lost problem people complain about is basically solved now. Which means the only thing left is a heartbreak of a story, art you'll screenshot constantly, and a score I still listen to while working. Play it now if the map scared you off at launch.

author: vinyl_and_vram
review_text: the soundtrack alone is worth the twenty euros. everything else is a bonus.

author: sequence_breaker
review_text: As someone who has finished basically every metroidvania worth playing: the movement kit here is top three ever. The Chandler fight forces you to use every tool you've unlocked and it's glorious. Ability gating is smart, secrets reward genuine curiosity, and yes, you can break the intended route in at least four places. The map deserved another design pass, but the world underneath it is exceptional.

author: one_evening_wonder
review_text: over in one evening, quoted at my office for a year.

author: drawbridge_dreamer
review_text:
Pros:
- total creative freedom, if you can draw it you can build it
- collapse physics that turn every siege into a demolition documentary
- the contract campaign has genuinely funny writing

Cons:
- stutters hard once builds get ambitious
- UI needs four clicks to place a single door
- no blueprint sharing yet

Recommended if your patience is as sturdy as your walls.

author: cv_padding_pro
review_text: i put this game on my CV under skills. got the job.

author: two_player_patience
review_text: My partner watches me play every night and we've named every crop plot. Would be a 10 if the promised co-op actually existed so she could join. Still waiting, Iron Petal.

author: salvage_squad_lead
review_text: Our Friday crew has cleared every wreck in the game and we love it, but you need to know about host migration: there isn't any, functionally. If the host's game closes, the session evaporates and everyone loses the haul. We solved it by making the guy with fiber internet the permanent host. That is not a real solution, Orbital Labs. Still recommended, because nothing else scratches this itch.

author: f13_survivor
review_text: i will never trust cell F13 again.

author: bailey_bottleneck
review_text: The stuttering is rhythmic at this point. Every time thirty peasants pathfind through the bailey at shift change, the game hiccups like it saw a ghost. Waited two patches for a fix, still juddering, thumb stays down.

author: mimic_flipper
review_text: Found the gold duplication trick by accident: sell a Mimic Chest to the pawn imp, buy it back, and it spits out double the coins every single time. By week 3 money completely stops mattering and the game becomes a joke dispenser. A very good joke dispenser, to be fair, so thumbs up, but the economy needs an actual patch and not vibes.

author: chromaburn
review_text: A year later and I still boot it up almost daily. Post-1.4 it's rock solid, the seasonal time trials keep it fresh, and I hold the Sunset Loop lap record among my friends, which they will never hear the end of.

author: tab_complete_speed
review_text: Found the tab-completion artifact on floor six and my runs got forty percent faster overnight. Speedrunning this game is typing practice with a body count. The no-tutorial complaints are fair, but the depth underneath is absurd.

author: CAPSLOCK_CASTAWAY
review_text: LOST SIX HOURS OF PROGRESS BECAUSE THE AUTOSAVE ATE MY RUN AT THE BRINEFALL. SIX. HOURS. THE FILE JUST SAYS 'DATA CORRUPTED'. I FOUGHT THE TIDEWALKER WITH ONE FLARE AND A PRAYER AND THE GAME COULD NOT BE BOTHERED TO REMEMBER IT. FIX YOUR SAVE SYSTEM BEFORE YOU SELL A HORROR GAME. THE REAL HORROR IS THE SAVE MENU.

author: roster_robbed
review_text: Base game ships with twelve units and the balance patch notes casually discuss units I do not even own. Half the depth costs extra. Quiet Signal makes brilliant games and hostile storefronts.

author: vinyl_moth
review_text: Bought the soundtrack before I even finished the game. The composer deserves every award that exists. The game attached to the music is also incredible.

author: nvme_nick
review_text: 45 second loads into every skirmish on a Samsung 980 Pro. An NVMe drive should not feel like a cassette tape. The game itself is superb once it finally lets you in.

author: rentmath_rob
review_text: The rent numbers make zero sense. A goblin in a broom closet pays 4000 gold a week while my dragon penthouse tenant pays 12. Twelve. The whole economy is held together with duct tape and jokes.

author: stone_by_stone
review_text: The May optimization patch roughly doubled my frame rate in big builds. It still dips when a wall comes down, but my thousand-piece citadel is finally playable instead of a screensaver. Faith restored, thumb flipped.

author: slideshow_sam
review_text: optimization is nonexistent. gorgeous castle, beautiful slideshow.

author: second_dive
review_text: Bought at launch, lost two runs to corrupted saves, shelved it in anger. Came back after patch 1.2 in January and it's a different game — thirty hours since, zero save issues, and they even added manual save slots as backup. Finally finished it. The Brinefall sequence is the best horror set piece I've ever played, full stop. If the save bug scared you off, it's safe to come back down.

author: couch_detectives
review_text: My partner and I play it together on the couch, arguing about suspects like an old married detective duo. We only needed a guide once, for the tram timetable. There is no hint system whatsoever, so bring a second brain.

author: done_waiting_dana
review_text: 62 hours, uninstalling with regret. Two things broke me: sitting through minute long loads between every skirmish on a brand new SSD, and watching the ranked meta drift toward DLC units I refuse to buy on principle. The core design deserves a monument. The product wrapped around it deserves a refund. When loads are fixed and units are earnable, I will return.

author: silent_credits
review_text: Solved the case at 2am and just sat there in the dark afterwards. No game has ever done that to me before.

author: twice_bitten
review_text: Corrupted save at hour twelve. Twice. I'm done.

author: tapestry_tactician
review_text: Discovered that a tapestry was the only thing holding up my banquet hall. Removed it during redecorating, the ceiling followed, and forty peasants filed a complaint. The physics engine is the best comedian in games right now.

author: nova_x2_owner
review_text: I get 15 fps standing in my own throne room. This is on a Nova X2 with 16 gigs of RAM, not some potato. There's no excuse for a building game where building things is the performance problem.

author: hotfix_hope
review_text: Patch 1.0.4 actually fixed the T-posing and my quest log finally makes sense. Coldsnap has been shipping fixes weekly. Cautiously flipping my review to positive, this is slowly becoming the game it promised to be.

author: familiar_stories
review_text: Every tenant has a whole life. The vampire requests blackout curtains via increasingly passive aggressive letters, the ghost pays rent early out of guilt, and the werewolf blames every full moon incident on his roommate. You renovate towers to unlock new tenant species and every single one is a comedy engine. The economy is broken, who cares, I am rich and laughing.

author: bunicuta_gamer
review_text: l-am luat pentru nepotu-miu si acum ne certam pe rand la PC. e genul de joc care te face sa zici "inca o runda" pana la 2 noaptea. dragalas rau, recomand cu incredere

author: placement_pain
review_text: My placement matches included two players with 900+ wins and a bot that resigned on move one. The rating system is held together with tape. Great concept, broken ladder.

author: gigaclub_gang
review_text: Our group has a standing Thursday reservation. The Gigaclub order with the timer at ten seconds remains the hardest thing we have done in any game: three breads, wrong cheese, someone crying with laughter, the fryer on fire. The chaos scales perfectly with player count and the unlockable kitchens keep it fresh. Speedrun Sandwich understands that comedy is timing.

author: twist_survivor
review_text: Wow. That's the review. (The twist, I mean. Wow.)

author: sendhelp_sower
review_text: 437 hours played. Not recommended. The devs vanished, the endgame is spreadsheet farming, and my real garden died because I was busy watering fake crops. Last night I set an alarm to harvest turnips that do not exist. I cannot stop playing. Send help.

author: three_hour_tour
review_text: Uninstalled after three hours. Best three hours of my year.

author: wrong_turn_wanda
review_text: No waypoints, no map pins, no fast travel for the first ten hours. I don't have the patience I had at nineteen. Beautiful game, but I bounced off hard.

author: engine_spotter
review_text: Obvious engine users in every other lobby. Nobody legitimately finds mate in twelve after four seconds of thinking, five games in a row. The report system does nothing.

author: credits_2h11m
review_text: Credits rolled at 2h11m and the second act clearly wanted more room to breathe. The haunting escalates beautifully and then just resolves. Great concept stretched thin. If they ever add a chapter I'll flip this thumb.

author: grpe_typo_club
review_text: i failed my first twenty runs because i kept typing grpe under pressure. the game does not forgive. i do not learn. 10/10

author: slurp_hero
review_text: Chill, cheap, and I dream about broth now. Buy it.

author: inkwing
review_text: Stopped mid-boss to stare at the background art. Died. Worth it.

author: slowburn_sensei
review_text: Not for the impatient, and I do not mean the load times, I mean the design. Missions reward planning three turns deep, and pulling off a perfect echo chain feels like composing music. For thinky players this is essential.

author: therapy_thistle
review_text: my therapist plays this too. we compare builds in session.

author: again_at_417
review_text: Finished it, immediately started over. It hits so different when you know.

author: shop_blind_sailor
review_text: Pretend the shop doesn't exist and this is the best naval combat around. Wind actually matters, boarding is chaotic joy, and the sea shanties slap. My crew of four has a standing Tuesday appointment.

author: moon_magnet
review_text: Died 400 times on Gravity Well 7. Regret nothing.

author: couch_captain
review_text: Four players, one kitchen, ninety seconds, a bread catapult. We screamed so much the neighbors checked on us. Best couch co-op purchase in years, and it is nine euro.

author: cubicle_cryptid
review_text: I've worked in offices for eleven years and this is the first horror game to understand that the genre was always about us. The haunting escalates through passive-aggressive cell comments, a shared file that is somehow always locked by someone named nobody, and a budget that balances itself if you stop watching. It's still short even with the free chapter, but I laughed, I gasped, and I filed the whole experience under miscellaneous expenses.
